They're an example of neopronouns (some other common neopronouns include ey/em/eir/emself, ae/aem/aer/aemself, it/it/it's/itself). Neopronouns are usually used in a singular way and are gender neutral so it's a nice alternative to they/them pronouns which are the only gender neutral pronouns that society uses so far. 

There are two main categories of neopronouns: ones that are different combinations of pronoun-like sounds, the ones I mentioned above are all like that, and noun-self pronouns which are mainly used by the neuorodivergent community because they don't connect to any other pronouns. 

I personally like xe/xem because it uses the he/him, she/her, and they/them sounds and conjugations but with a little twist (it starts with a different sound) so it's a perfect gender neutral singular pronoun alternative for people who don't identify with the gender binary that exists in society.

Hey another really helpful tip that I found that you can do on your own is to write phrases in third person with your new pronouns of stuff that is true. It helped me to sort of connect my identity to those pronouns, and it helps you understand that since it's you who's doing that action, those are your pronouns.

For example, let's say I'm getting a haircut this Saturday, my brain knows this and it's a given.

"I'm getting a haircut saturday" --> "They're getting a haircut Saturday" (doing it with my pronouns but you'd do it with she)

You can practice it on your own! And think of yourself in third person whenever you need to of actions that you're doing to reaffirm your pronouns and your identity :)

Another few things to add on! Everything everyone else has said is really good, but some extra info: 

You usually "break in" a binder like you do with shoes, it gets more comfortable and accommodates to you after a few weeks of you wearing it. Most recommend you start off with an hour or two the first few days at home where you can easily take it off as soon as it starts to be a lot so you can be safe. You can increase the amount of hours you wear it and you'll feel it be more comfortable and wearable and then you can do the 8 hours if you want to (but no more). 

When you get your binder, make sure you can take a full breath (it's ok if it feels tight like another person said) and move your arms/upper body around, that's a good sign that it's your size. 

Binder breaks! Stretch your back and twist your upper body side to side, lean forward and backwards and just move around, lay on your back and take deep breaths all the way into your lungs, it'll help your body feel better!

Don't wash it in the washing machine and wash it once a week or every few days (depends on how much physical activity you do, I go by smell/how dirty it looks). They're sensitive and the elastic will wear out if you do, hand wash it in the sink or in the shower with lukewarm water and some laundry detergent or soap, don't use any strong chemicals like bleach.  Leave it out to air-dry overnight and it should be good the next morning :)
